name: Chesapeake Bay Small Watershed Grants
summary: Annual NFWF grants, funded mainly by the US EPA, for community-based projects that protect and restore water quality and habitat in the Chesapeake Bay watershed. Implementation grants fund on-the-ground work; smaller planning and technical assistance grants prepare future projects.

amount.note: Implementation grants; planning and technical assistance grants go up to $150,000

reporting: Grantees choose the most relevant project metrics from NFWF's list in Easygrants and report against them.

eligibility.rule: Projects begin on or after September 1, 2026
No NFWF funds for ongoing legal compliance efforts
Stream and floodplain restoration follows CBP qualifying conditions and protocols
State agencies and higher education institutions document partner support for PTA proposals
Applicants with active NFWF grants are in good standing

documents: Stream and Floodplain Restoration Narrative Supplement, for stream restoration and floodplain reconnection projects
Letters of support from community partners and/or collaborators
Statement of Litigation, unless a government applicant
Board member list, or statement that no Board exists

geography.quote: All projects must occur wholly within the Chesapeake Bay watershed.

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

amount.quote: SWG Implementation (SWG-I) grants of $150,000-750,000 will be awarded for projects that result in direct, on-the-ground actions to protect and restore water quality, species, and habitats in the Bay watershed.

co_finance_required.quote: non-federal matching funds are encouraged but not required.

reporting.quote: the Chesapeake Bay Stewardship Fund has a list of metrics in Easygrants for proposal applicants to choose from for future reporting

window.quote: Proposal Due Date Thursday, April 2, 12:00 PM ET

eligibility.quote: All proposed projects must begin on or after September 1, 2026, to facilitate necessary grant contracting, quality assurance, and environmental compliance activities.
NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlement agreements.

Proposed stream and floodplain restoration efforts must be consistent with qualifying conditions for nutrient and sediment load reductions under the Chesapeake Bay TMDL and associated design and crediting protocols established by the CBP partnership

State government agencies and institutions of higher education are eligible to apply for Planning and Technical Assistance proposals but must document support and/or request for proposed activities by appropriate non-profit organizations, local and municipal governments, Tribal governments and organizations and/or K-12 education institutions.
All applicants with active grants from NFWF must be in good standing in terms of reporting requirements, expenditure of funds, and quality assurance (if required).

after_award.quote: Grantees will update FieldDoc to show project progress prior to each Interim and Final Programmatic Report

documents.quote: Applicants for stream restoration and floodplain reconnection projects must complete and upload an accompanying "Stream and Floodplain Restoration Narrative Supplement" in addition to the required full proposal narrative.
submit letters of support from community partners and/or collaborators demonstrating their commitment to the project and engagement in project activities as proposed.
